title: Prison Study: Evidence, Mechanisms, and Ethics
sourceLabel: 既存教材をTOEFL形式へ変換 · 元の問1–9に対応
verificationNote: 四つの原文段落と全九つの学習対象を保持し、元の記述問題を英語四択へ変換しました。

passages.text:
In 1971 a simulated prison study assigned a small group of male college students to prisoner and guard roles. Distress and degrading conduct occurred, and the study ended after six days rather than the planned two weeks. The episode became a widely repeated illustration of how institutional roles and unequal power can shape behavior. Its dramatic narrative made it memorable, but memorability is not a measure of evidential strength.

Random assignment helps reduce pre-existing differences between groups, yet it cannot by itself create a clean experiment. There was no ordinary neutral control condition, the sample was narrow, the researchers also managed the simulation, and expectations may have influenced conduct. Archival work has reported that at least some guards received direction about producing a tough environment and that behavior varied considerably among guards. These details complicate the claim that role assignment alone generated a uniform response.

Methodological criticism does not prove that situations are powerless. It changes the question. Instead of asking whether “good people automatically become cruel,” researchers can examine which instructions, norms, monitoring failures, incentives, identities, and opportunities permit abuse. This formulation treats situation as a set of measurable mechanisms rather than a mysterious force.

Ethical evaluation is also essential. Participation should involve meaningful consent, protection from avoidable harm, and a genuine ability to withdraw. When investigators occupy operational roles, their duty to observe harm can conflict with their investment in continuing the study. The lasting lesson is therefore not one simple result. It is that researchers must study power without reproducing unchecked power inside research itself.

questions.prompt: What is the main idea of the passage?

options.label: A
options.text: The study conclusively proved that every person becomes cruel when assigned power.

options.label: B
options.text: The study's dramatic lesson must be evaluated through design limits, behavioral variation, mechanisms, and ethics.

options.label: C
options.text: Random assignment made every other feature of the study scientifically irrelevant.

options.label: D
options.text: Ethical concerns matter only after a study has produced a uniform result.

questions.answer: 正解：B。本文は印象的な物語をそのまま強い証拠とせず、設計上の限界、行動のばらつき、具体的機序、研究倫理から再評価します。A・C・Dは本文が退ける単純化です。

questions.prompt: Which statement correctly distinguishes reported facts from an interpretation of the study?

options.label: A
options.text: Distress occurred and the study ended after six days are reported facts; roles and unequal power shaped behavior is an interpretation.

options.label: B
options.text: Every guard behaved identically is a fact; the study lasted six days is an interpretation.

options.label: C
options.text: The sample was broad is a fact; no participant experienced distress is an interpretation.

options.label: D
options.text: Role assignment alone caused cruelty is a fact; random assignment occurred is merely an opinion.

questions.answer: 正解：A。苦痛・品位を傷つける行為と6日での終了は観察報告で、制度的役割と権力が行動を形作ったという説明は解釈です。B～Dは本文の事実と推論を逆転・捏造しています。

questions.prompt: The phrase “complicate the claim” in paragraph 2 most nearly means

options.label: A
options.text: prove the claim without any remaining uncertainty

options.label: B
options.text: require the claim to be qualified or supplemented by additional explanations

options.label: C
options.text: make the claim easier to memorize

options.label: D
options.text: show that all situational influences are powerless

questions.answer: 正解：B。指示の存在と警備役間の差は「役割だけが一様な反応を生んだ」という主張に限定や追加説明を必要とさせます。完全証明や状況要因の全面否定ではありません。

questions.prompt: What can random assignment accomplish, and what can it not accomplish here?

options.label: A
options.text: It can reduce pre-existing group differences, but it cannot fix a narrow sample, absent neutral control, researcher involvement, or expectation effects.

options.label: B
options.text: It can guarantee a representative sample and remove every influence from researchers.

options.label: C
options.text: It can create a neutral control condition even when none was included.

options.label: D
options.text: It cannot reduce group differences, but it can prove that all guards respond uniformly.

questions.answer: 正解：A。無作為割付は事前差を平均的に減らしますが、標本の狭さ、対照条件の欠如、研究者の運営参加、期待効果までは解決しません。B～Dは割付の機能を誇張または否定します。

questions.prompt: Why do directions to guards and expectations threaten the claim that role assignment alone caused the conduct?

options.label: A
options.text: They confound the effect of the assigned role with responses to investigator demands.

options.label: B
options.text: They prove that no guard received an assigned role.

options.label: C
options.text: They make the sample representative of the entire population.

options.label: D
options.text: They create an ordinary neutral control group.

questions.answer: 正解：A。厳しい環境を作るよう求められたなら、行動は役割そのものだけでなく研究者の要求への反応かもしれず、因果要因が交絡します。B～Dは本文と矛盾します。

questions.prompt: What can be inferred from the passage's revised account of situational influence?

options.label: A
options.text: A situation must operate as one mysterious and indivisible force.

options.label: B
options.text: Situational influence can be decomposed into testable mechanisms such as instructions, norms, incentives, and monitoring.

options.label: C
options.text: Methodological criticism proves that power never affects behavior.

options.label: D
options.text: Individual identity is the only mechanism worth examining.

questions.answer: 正解：B。本文は「状況」を神秘的な一因ではなく、指示、規範、監視の失敗、誘因、同一化、機会という測定可能な機序へ分解します。A・C・Dはこの再定式化に反します。

questions.prompt: What problem arises when investigators also manage the simulated prison?

options.label: A
options.text: Their investment in continuing may conflict with their duty to notice and stop harm, while also influencing behavior.

options.label: B
options.text: Their operational role guarantees complete neutrality.

options.label: C
options.text: Their involvement makes informed consent unnecessary.

options.label: D
options.text: Their management automatically creates a broad sample.

questions.answer: 正解：A。運営者と観察者を兼ねると、継続への関与が危害を察知・停止する義務と衝突し、同時に研究対象の行動にも影響します。B～Dは倫理・方法上の問題を逆に表現します。

questions.prompt: What does the final statement about studying power without reproducing unchecked power emphasize?

options.label: A
options.text: Research on abuse may itself recreate the dangerous power relations it seeks to understand unless authority is constrained.

options.label: B
options.text: Researchers should exercise unlimited authority to make simulations realistic.

options.label: C
options.text: Power can be studied only by eliminating participant withdrawal.

options.label: D
options.text: Ethical safeguards prevent any meaningful study of institutions.

questions.answer: 正解：A。権力濫用を研究する場そのものに無制限な権力を作れば、研究目的と倫理が自己矛盾します。B・Cはその危険を推奨し、Dは保護と研究を誤って二者択一にします。

questions.prompt: Which revision best replaces the claim that assigned roles inevitably make good people cruel?

options.label: A
options.text: Under particular roles, instructions, expectations, and weak safeguards, some participants may act abusively; the narrow sample and varied behavior require mechanism-focused, ethical tests.

options.label: B
options.text: The six-day study proves that all people in every institution respond in exactly the same way.

options.label: C
options.text: Because the design had limitations, situations and power can never influence conduct.

options.label: D
options.text: The original claim needs no qualification because dramatic evidence is always strong evidence.

questions.answer: 正解：A。小さく限定的な標本、警備役間の差、指示を示す資料を踏まえ、必然性ではなく条件付きの機序へ主張を直し、倫理的設計で検証します。B～Dは過度の一般化か全面否定です。
